The Kogi State Police Command has defended firearms training organised by the state Vigilante Service for members of its Mining and Boundary Vigilante Group in Ankpa Local Government Area, dismissing claims that the exercise was politically motivated.
The command said preliminary investigations established that the training was legitimate and intended to improve the handling and use of newly acquired firearms by the vigilante personnel.
In a statement on Sunday, the police spokesperson, Saliu Afusat, said the four-day exercise had been communicated to relevant security authorities before it began. The command also said it had received details of the training and the names and photographs of personnel selected to participate.
The clarification followed the circulation of a video on social media alleging that some individuals were being trained to use firearms for political purposes in Ankpa.
The police said the person who recorded the video explained during preliminary interviews that he wanted to draw the attention of security agencies to the exercise to establish its legitimacy.
The command acknowledged the importance of public vigilance but urged residents to verify security-related information before sharing it, warning that unverified claims could cause panic and public unrest.
The latest clarification comes days after the police addressed another viral video circulating on social media, captioned “Police Don Buy Soja Job”.

In a statement issued on 6 November, the command said the footage showed an incident during the 2023 Kogi State governorship election and did not depict a recent occurrence.
According to the police, the video showed officers attached to the then Deputy Speaker of the Kogi State House of Assembly, Ahmed Ahmed, who had accompanied him to his hometown, Abache, to vote.
Military personnel deployed for election duties arrested the officers in connection with the enforcement of the restriction of movement, the command said.
The officers were taken into custody, and the matter was transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department for investigation.
The police command said the circulation of the old footage without its historical context could create distrust between security agencies.
It also emphasised that the command maintained cooperation with the military and other security agencies in the state.
In its latest statement, the command again acknowledged the role of the Kogi State Vigilante Service in security operations and said its activities should be properly monitored and conducted within the law.
